body:
piotr: heads-up, we're seeing sustained queue growth on gpu-pool-eu-west-1 starting ~30m ago. autoscaler didn't add nodes, multiple customer requests timing out. paging now.

pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT CREATED - high GPU queue depth (gpu-pool-eu-west-1). Priority: P1. Notifying oncall.

ryan-oncall: I'm on it. grabbing metrics. what's the highest queue depth?

maya: peak ~520 pending tokens across pool, average latency >2.4s for token generation, error rate up for a handful of heavy prompt routes. see chart: https://grafana.redwood/g/dash/pool-eu-west-1

ops-jen: autoscaler logs show repeated attempts to scale but failing with "scale quota hit" and "pool provisioning timeout". also noticed continuous-batching reduced active batch window in last deploy.

eng-runtime: that deploy was the batching/caching tunables roll (PR #9123) earlier today. we lowered prefix_cache_ttl from 10m -> 30s to free memory for other pools. could be evictions causing re-population overhead.

piotr: if prefix cache miss rate spiked we'll be redoing KV cache priming on every request which is expensive. can someone dump prefix cache hitrate?

sam-sre: running quick query: prefix_cache_hit_rate{pool="gpu-pool-eu-west-1"} jumped from 96% -> 12% around 1856787000. TTLs look... wrong.

support-alex: multiple customers reporting 502/timeouts: CUST-1012, CUST-2027. flagged with Priority support.

ryan-oncall: OK mitigation plan: 1) stop new long-running routes (apply temporary route throttle), 2) increase pool capacity if possible, 3) revert prefix_cache_ttl or bump it, 4) rollback batching window tweak if it reduces batching efficiency.

maya: applying route throttle now for routes: /v1/generate-heavy, /v1/chat-heavy. Command: 
```
# temporarily set rate limit to 5rps for heavy routes
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://api.redwood/internal/config/routes/throttle -d '{"route": "/v1/generate-heavy","limit":5}'
```

piotr: throttle applied. incoming qps reduced by ~18% already.

eng-runtime: autoscaler error details: "scale_request rejected: account max_gpus=40, requested 52". Dedicated pools hitting account quota. Can we borrow from spare capacity in shared pool?

ops-jen: opening quota bump with infra but that's slow. short-term: bring up standby smaller instances in a new transient pool with the same serving runtime. spinning them up now with terraform apply --var transient=true

sam-sre: watch: new pool startup failing due to container image pull rate limits -> fixed by switching to internal registry mirror. retrying.

pagerduty-bot: Pager escalated to engineering lead.

eng-runtime: while infra works on capacity, we should revert prefix_cache_ttl to previous safe value 600s. I'll patch config and roll to all nodes.

piotr: please confirm the exact config change. current in etcd: continuous_batch_window_ms=12 -> 8 and prefix_cache_ttl_s=30. We want prefix_cache_ttl_s=600 and continuous_batch_window_ms back to 12.

eng-runtime: applying config patch: 
```
kubectl patch configmap/runtime-tunables -n inference -p '{"data":{"prefix_cache_ttl_s":"600","continuous_batch_window_ms":"12"}}'
```

eng-runtime: rolling restart queued for runtime pods. doing a 3x rolling restart to avoid spike.

sam-sre: note: rolling restart will temporarily reduce available GPUs for a few minutes per pod; coordinate with capacity add.

ops-jen: transient pool coming up. currently 6/8 instances ready. they should accept traffic once routing updated.

support-alex: letting customers CUST-1012 and CUST-2027 know we're mitigating and ETA ~30-45m. sent update.

maya: prefix cache hit rate recovering slowly, now 42% and climbing. queue length decreasing to ~220. token latency trending down to 1.1s.

ryan-oncall: good. continue monitoring. any errors from autoscaler now?

ops-jen: autoscaler requests queued; now allowed to add 10 more GPUs after we freed up quotas by moving some non-critical workloads. scale events successful.

eng-runtime: continuous batching rollback applied. batch window back to 12ms. this increased synchronous batching efficiency — expect fewer tiny batches.

piotr: after these changes, KV cache priming CPU overhead dropped ~55% on sample nodes. throughput per GPU up ~30%.

pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED - mitigation applied: throttle, prefix cache TTL rollback, batching rollback, transient pool + autoscaler scale. Customer impact reduced.

sam-sre: moving to Handoff -> followups. can the oncall finish postmortem template?

ryan-oncall: I'll take the handoff. current state: pools stable, queues at normal levels, no further customer 502s in last 12m. leaving monitoring for next 2h.

eng-runtime: immediate root cause (working hypothesis): aggressive prefix_cache_ttl reduction + batching window tweak in morning deploy increased cache miss rate and reduced batching efficiency. That combo multiplied per-request overhead and pushed queue length up. Autoscaler couldn't provision beyond account quota which amplified customer impact.

piotr: action items (short):
- eng-runtime: revert tuning (done) and add safety guard in deploy pipeline to prevent prefix_cache_ttl < 300s for GPU pools
- infra: review account GPU quotas and set alert when usage > 85%
- autoscaler: surface clearer rejection reason to incident logs when quota blocks scaling
- oncall/sre: run a chaos test for cache eviction scenarios

support-alex: updated customers with incident summary + mitigation steps; asked if they saw data loss (none reported).

ryan-oncall: handing off to day team with summary and timeline. leaving note to schedule postmortem meeting tomorrow 10:00 UTC.

pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED - status: mitigated. Please file postmortem under incidents/ postmortems.

sam-sre: opened follow-up ticket FT-3312 for guarding tunables in deploy pipeline.

maya: thanks team. small ask: can we add a dashboard panel that correlates prefix cache hit rate + request queue depth + scale rejection reasons for faster triage?

eng-runtime: will do. assigning to me and piotr.

piotr: closing thread from oncall handoff perspective. leaving logs and grep commands used below for postmortem: 
```
grafana query: sum(rate(kv_cache_repopulate{pool="gpu-pool-eu-west-1"}[1m])) by (instance)
kubectl logs deploy/autoscaler -n infra | grep "scale_request rejected" --context=2
```

sam-sre: thanks. filing final incident report.

ryan-oncall: ending watch. back to normal ops. :white_check_mark:
